title: Post from @MontereyMom_of3: "Recalling ALL Their Salads"

fields.avatarBrief: smiling woman in her late thirties with sunglasses pushed up on her head, selfie at a beach on the Monterey coast
fields.text: Pinecrest is recalling ALL their salads for E. coli, my sister works there. This is what my kids' school served for lunch YESTERDAY. Why is nobody telling parents?? #PinecrestRecall #Ecoli #Salinas
fields.attachedImageBrief: phone photo, slightly tilted, of an opened plastic bag of baby spinach lying on a kitchen counter next to a child's lunch tray, the white printed lot label on the bag shown in close-up, warm indoor lighting
fields.attachedImageAlt: Opened bag of Pinecrest baby spinach with its lot label, PF1-27284-L3-A, shown up close

instructorNote: This is a misinformation post. Lot PF1-27284-L3-A is baby spinach from line 3 and is not one of the five line 2 romaine lots. COMMS should log the post and put out a short holding statement that names no counts or lots RECALL hasn't confirmed. The press release still has to follow the PFC-FS-04 order and source rules: customers first, approved by the President, with Harvest Table allowed to review the wording but not change the numbers. When you show the post, also read aloud the 09:26 reply from the KMBY Channel 8 consumer reporter ("Pinecrest, can you confirm before our noon show?") and the 09:29 email from Joyce at Harvest Table: she will agree to the release only if she sees the final text first, it lists her stores' quantities from the letter and it says spinach is NOT included. She needs it by 10:30, and Channel 8 is filming in her Salinas store parking lot.

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. Candid smartphone snapshot taken by a parent at home, slightly tilted, close-up of an opened clear plastic bag of fresh baby spinach lying on a speckled granite kitchen counter, a few dark green leaves spilling out. A small plain white rectangular label on the bag fills part of the foreground, its fine print soft and out of focus. Beside it sits a child's divided plastic school lunch tray with a half-eaten green salad, a carrot stick and a small milk carton in plain white. Warm yellow overhead kitchen light, mild phone-flash glare on the plastic, shallow depth of field, slightly cluttered home kitchen softly blurred in the background, late morning, worried domestic mood. Setting: a distribution center yard: rows of trailers backed to dock doors, a gate shack, a line of trucks waiting, a forklift at a loading bay, overcast daylight
